faq.q: What is the smallest rural lot I can create in the Township?
faq.a: It depends on the zone under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, s. 110.1: RU-1 requires 1.7 ha for a new lot, RU-2 and RU-3 require 8.0 ha, SR-2 requires 8,094 m² and SR-1 requires 3,716 m² — and ALR land also needs Agricultural Land Commission permission to subdivide.

faq.q: Who approves a subdivision in Langley?
faq.a: The Approving Officer, as required under the Land Title Act — in the Township the process runs application, review, decision letter, conditions, final approval and registration in the Land Title Office; in the City, Bylaw 3300 adds that meeting the minimum lot standards does not bind the Approving Officer to approve.

faq.q: Can I build a second home on a rural Langley lot?
faq.a: On ALR land, one additional detached residence is permitted without an ALC application where the conditions are met — 90 m² or less on parcels of 40 ha or smaller, 186 m² or less on larger parcels — and Township bylaws must also permit it; the principal residence is capped at 500 m².
